questions.prompt: Why should you use `YAML.safe_load` (or `JSON.parse`) instead of `Marshal.load` or `YAML.load` on untrusted input?

options.text: `Marshal.load` and unsafe `YAML.load` can instantiate arbitrary Ruby objects and trigger remote code execution

questions.prompt: Why does `# frozen_string_literal: true` at the top of Ruby files improve memory and GC performance?

options.text: String literals are reused as single frozen objects instead of allocating a new `String` on every loop/method call

questions.prompt: What is MRI (CRuby)'s Global VM Lock (GVL) limitation for `Thread.new`?

options.text: Only one thread executes Ruby code at a time per process, though threads release the GVL while waiting on blocking I/O

questions.prompt: Match each Ruby concurrency/parallelism tool to its best fit.

columns.label: Concurrent blocking I/O (HTTP/DB) when libraries release the GVL
True multi-core CPU parallelism and isolated memory
Lightweight cooperative concurrency for high-connection I/O

questions.prompt: What is an N+1 query bug in Rails/ActiveRecord, and how is it fixed?

options.text: Loading N parent records and firing 1 extra SQL query per parent in a loop; fix with eager loading (`includes` / `preload`)

questions.prompt: Select all practices that prevent SQL injection and mass-assignment bugs in Ruby web apps. (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Permit only expected attributes with Strong Parameters (`params.expect(...)` / `permit(...)`)
Interpolate `params[:sort]` directly into `order("#{params[:sort]}")` without an allowlist
Use parameterized queries (`User.where("email = ?", email)` or hash conditions)

questions.prompt: Why is `"a" + "b"` in a tight loop slower than `String#<<` (or `Array#join`) when building a large string?

options.text: `+` allocates a brand-new string on every concatenation, whereas `<<` mutates a single buffer

questions.prompt: What does `respond_to_missing?(name, include_private = false)` need to accompany `method_missing`?
Why are Refinements (`using MyRefinement`) safer than global monkey-patching (`class String; def ...; end`)?

options.text: Refinements scope method additions/overrides lexically to the current file/module instead of mutating classes globally

questions.prompt: What does `SecureRandom.urlsafe_base64(32)` provide compared to `rand`?

options.text: Cryptographically strong random tokens safe for session IDs, API keys, and CSRF tokens

questions.prompt: Select all practices that keep Ruby test suites (RSpec / Minitest) fast and reliable. (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Stub external HTTP APIs (e.g., WebMock / VCR) instead of hitting live networks in unit tests
Keep unit tests pure and reserve full DB/browser integration tests for critical flows
Use `freeze`/isolated test data rather than shared mutable globals
Sleep for 5 seconds in every test to wait for threads

questions.prompt: What is a common memory leak when storing request-specific data in a `Thread.current[:key]` or class variable `@@cache`?

options.text: `Thread.current` is cleared on every method return
In pooled servers (Puma/Sidekiq), threads and classes live across requests, retaining stale user data or unbounded caches

questions.prompt: What does `Rack` provide in the Ruby web ecosystem?

options.text: A minimal, standardized HTTP interface (`call(env) -> [status, headers, body]`) connecting Ruby frameworks (Rails, Sinatra) to servers (Puma)

questions.prompt: Why should production Ruby web servers (like Puma) enforce request/DB/HTTP timeouts?

options.text: Without explicit timeouts on `Net::HTTP` or external APIs, slow upstreams tie up all worker threads/processes and cause cascading outages
Puma disables timeouts by default on `puts`

questions.prompt: Match each Ruby performance or reliability tool to its role.

columns.label: In-process JIT compiler accelerating production Ruby throughput
Static style, lint, and performance/security cop checker
Static security vulnerability scanner for Rails apps

questions.prompt: What does `ObjectSpace.memsize_of` / memory profilers help diagnose in long-running Ruby workers?

options.text: Retained object allocations and memory bloat from large closures, unclosed streams, or unbounded caches

questions.prompt: Why can capturing a huge local variable inside a returned `Proc` or `lambda` retain memory unexpectedly?

options.text: Closures capture their surrounding `Binding`, keeping referenced objects alive as long as the `Proc` is alive

questions.prompt: What does `Integer(input)` do differently from `input.to_i` when validating user input `"12abc"`?
Select all valid reasons to use `Enumerable#lazy` or `IO.foreach` when processing a 5 GB CSV/log file.

options.text: Reads one line at a time with O(1) memory instead of `File.read` loading 5 GB into RAM
Allows early termination with `.first(10)` without scanning the rest of the file

questions.prompt: What is the risk of `const_get(user_input)` or `public_send(user_input)` on unsanitized user parameters?

options.text: Attackers can invoke unintended methods or access arbitrary constants unless `user_input` is checked against an explicit allowlist

questions.prompt: Why should `bundle audit` (or Dependabot) be part of Ruby CI?

options.text: To detect gems in `Gemfile.lock` with known published security advisories (CVEs)

questions.prompt: Match each Ruby security pitfall to its safe mitigation.

columns.label: Check `params[:act]` against an allowlist and use `public_send`

questions.prompt: In Ruby, why is `BigDecimal` preferred over `Float` for currency and financial totals?

options.text: `Float` uses binary floating point (`0.1 + 0.2 != 0.3`), whereas `BigDecimal` performs exact base-10 arithmetic

questions.prompt: What does `Signal.trap("TERM")` allow a long-running Ruby worker or daemon to do?

options.text: Initiate graceful shutdown (finish current job, close DB connections, flush logs) when orchestrated containers stop it

questions.prompt: Select all statements that are true about Ruby `Fiber`s and `Ractor`s. (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Non-blocking Fiber schedulers can multiplex thousands of I/O operations on one thread
`Ractor`s share all mutable global hashes freely without copying
`Fiber`s provide lightweight cooperative concurrency with manual or scheduler-driven yielding
`Ractor`s (Ruby 3+) run in parallel without sharing the GVL by isolating mutable state via message passing

questions.prompt: Why is `rescue => e` followed by `raise` (or structured logging + metrics) better than `rescue; nil; end`?

options.text: Silent `rescue nil` swallows bugs, DB outages, and data corruption without any trace

questions.prompt: What does `Time.utc` / `Time.now.utc` (or `ActiveSupport::TimeZone`) prevent in distributed Ruby backends?

options.text: Timezone drift and DST bugs across servers in different regions

questions.prompt: What does `Enumerator.new { |y| ... }` allow you to implement cleanly?

options.text: A custom lazy stream/generator producing values on demand via `y << item`

questions.prompt: Why should `Gemfile` specify pessimistic version constraints (`~> 2.1`) or lock with `Gemfile.lock`?

options.text: To allow compatible patch/minor updates while protecting against breaking major version jumps

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of `RBS` / `Sorbet` in large Ruby codebases?

options.text: Adding static type signatures and type checking to catch interface mismatches before runtime

questions.prompt: Match each Ruby backend reliability practice to what it prevents.

columns.label: Duplicate charges/emails when a job retries after transient failure
Worker threads hanging indefinitely on unresponsive upstreams
Exhausting DB/Redis connections under concurrent load

questions.prompt: Why is `Dir.mktmpdir` (with a block) preferred over hardcoding `"/tmp/work"` in Ruby scripts?

options.text: Hardcoded `/tmp` paths fail on Windows, collide across concurrent runs, and risk symlink attacks

questions.prompt: Select all valid ways to avoid mutating caller arguments unexpectedly in Ruby methods. (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Call `.dup` before mutating a local copy if needed
Always mutate the caller's passed-in `Hash` without documenting it
Use non-bang methods (`map`, `select`, `merge`) that return new objects

questions.prompt: What does `GC.stat` expose in Ruby?

options.text: Runtime garbage-collector metrics (heap slots, major/minor GC counts, allocated objects) for observability

questions.prompt: Why should `File.join(dir, filename)` (or `Pathname#join`) be used instead of `"#{dir}/#{filename}"`?

options.text: It normalizes separators portably across POSIX and Windows without double slashes
String interpolation doesn't work for paths

questions.prompt: How do you prevent path traversal when serving a user-requested file `name` inside `base_dir` in Ruby?

options.text: Expand both paths (`File.realpath` / `File.expand_path`) and verify the target starts with `base_dir + File::SEPARATOR`

questions.prompt: What does `Object#freeze` on a nested config `CONFIG = { hosts: ["a"] }.freeze` NOT protect?

options.text: Mutating the inner array `CONFIG[:hosts] << "b"` unless the inner array and strings are also frozen

questions.prompt: Select all practices that belong in a production Ruby CI pipeline. (Select all that apply.)

options.text: `bundle exec rubocop` for lint and style checks
`bundle exec rspec` / `rake test` for automated tests
`bundle exec bundler-audit check --update` for gem CVEs

questions.prompt: Why is structured JSON logging (e.g., Semantic Logger) preferred over raw `puts` in production Ruby services?

options.text: Structured logs include request IDs, severity levels, timestamps, and machine-parseable fields for log aggregation

questions.prompt: What does `at_exit { ... }` register in a Ruby process?

options.text: A hook executed when the Ruby process is exiting normally

questions.prompt: When should you prefer `Hash#fetch(:key)` over `hash[:key]`?

options.text: When missing keys should silently be `nil`
When a missing required key is a bug or configuration error that should fail fast with `KeyError`

questions.prompt: Match each Ruby production diagnostic to its cause.

rows.label: Dozens of identical `SELECT` queries per request
